s1.syndrome_frame: Worsening skin condition with systemic symptoms in a patient with a history of autoimmune disorders
salient_findings: Diffuse ill-defined erythema and mild edema of the face and eyelids
Violaceous to erythematous patches on the joints, periungual skin, and chest
Fatigue and difficulty with physical activities
key_facts: Patient has a history of biopsy-proven psoriasis
Patient has a history of juvenile dermatomyositis (DM)
Juvenile DM had been in remission for several years
Previous treatments included adalimumab, etanercept, methotrexate, guselkumab, ustekinumab, and topical corticosteroids
DM had remained stable during treatment with anti-TNF and anti-IL-12/23 medications
Patient experienced fatigue, difficulty picking up her child, and climbing stairs after starting new medication
Physical examination revealed diffuse ill-defined erythema and mild edema of the face and eyelids
Laboratory evaluation results were negative or normal, including creatine kinase and aldolase levels

shortlist.label: Dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of biopsy-proven juvenile dermatomyositis and is experiencing worsening skin condition with systemic symptoms

shortlist.label: Psoriasis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of biopsy-proven psoriasis and is experiencing worsening skin condition

shortlist.label: Lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is experiencing systemic symptoms and skin condition, which are common in lupus erythematosus

shortlist.label: Mixed connective tissue disease
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of autoimmune disorders and is experiencing overlapping symptoms of different diseases

shortlist.label: Polymyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is experiencing muscle weakness and skin condition, which are common in polymyositis

raw.rationale: The patient's history of biopsy-proven juvenile dermatomyositis, along with the presence of characteristic skin findings such as violaceous to erythematous patches on the joints and photodistributed poikiloderma, supports this diagnosis. Additionally, the patient's symptoms of fatigue and difficulty with physical activities after starting new medication could indicate a flare of her dermatomyositis.

rejected.label: Psoriasis
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of biopsy-proven psoriasis, the current presentation of skin findings and symptoms is more consistent with a flare of dermatomyositis.

rejected.label: Lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: There is no mention of specific criteria or symptoms that are characteristic of lupus erythematosus, such as malar rash, oral ulcers, or renal involvement.

rejected.label: Mixed connective tissue disease
rejected.why: The patient's presentation does not meet the criteria for mixed connective tissue disease, which typically includes a combination of features from multiple autoimmune diseases.

rejected.label: Polymyositis
rejected.why: The patient's skin findings are more consistent with dermatomyositis, and there is no mention of muscle biopsy results or other specific criteria that would support a diagnosis of polymyositis.
